Replay

ICE settings for party and Room connections

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Supplying settingsReachability and limits

Use Party_Config.ice_json to configure STUN discovery and TURN relay services for RTC connections. ICE is WebRTC's process for selecting a reachable connection path. The field supplies a bounded RTC configuration, copied when Party opens and carried into Room_Options.session.rtc.ice_json. Room keeps that copy through authority changes and reconnects. Direct Rtc_Config / Session_Options users can continue supplying ice_json themselves. An empty value retains the local-only default with no ICE servers.

The validator rejects oversized/deep JSON, non-dictionary roots, invalid server arrays, malformed URLs, missing TURN username/password fields and invalid transport policies before opening signaling. It allows at most 8 servers, 8 URLs per server and 8192 JSON bytes. URLs use stun:, stuns:, turn: or turns: with bounded host/port and optional TURN UDP/TCP transport. Other RTCConfiguration fields are passed to the platform; this validator does not certify arbitrary platform options.

Relay-only mode requires at least one authenticated TURN entry:

JSON
{
  "iceTransportPolicy": "relay",
  "iceServers": [{
    "urls": ["turn:relay.example.com:3478?transport=udp"],
    "username": "issued-user",
    "credential": "issued-password"
  }]
}

Godot forwards the configuration dictionary into its browser peer-connection constructor. Relay-only selection is a browser policy; the test harness verifies the actual selected pair rather than treating the configuration alone as evidence. Godot implementation, WebRTC configuration.

Supplying settings#

Native Cavecrawl reads REPLAY_CAVE_ICE_JSON; native Scrapyard reads RSY_ICE_JSON. These settings matter when using a native RTC extension; ordinary native ENet does not gain NAT traversal from an ICE configuration.

Browser hosts set globalThis.replayIceConfig before starting Godot. It may be the configuration object or its JSON string. The game calls rtc_ice_settings, validates and copies the value during setup. It is intentionally not read from URL query parameters, party invitations or saved enrollment records.

The optional authenticated relay provider mints short-lived TURN credentials for enrolled members. Party_Config.relay_credentials enables background refresh and a source that refuses expired credentials when building new connections. Static ICE JSON remains available for other provider channels. Never ship the provider's shared signing secret to clients. In-place ICE restart, broader expiry/outage combinations and public deployment remain separate integration work.

The configuration is runtime connection data, not gameplay state. It does not enter authority checkpoints, recipient snapshots, saved progression or invitation codes. Errors shown by the games describe the configuration failure without echoing the JSON. The configuration's strings are owned by Party/Room/Rtc for their respective lifetimes; changing the caller's original buffer cannot alter a live configuration.

Same-term gameplay reconnect retains the authenticated RTC reservation in memory when scope/incarnation match. Actual relay-stop/restart gates preserve the logical peer ID and action ledger while rebuilding data channels. See RTC recovery. This does not renew expired TURN credentials.

Reachability and limits#

Actual Coturn UDP and TCP relay fixtures exercise party gameplay, handoff and rejoin. The authentication fixture proves a bad password cannot silently fall back to a direct candidate when relay-only mode is selected. See relay tests and recorded evidence.

These local tests are not public Internet deployment acceptance. Public DNS, HTTPS/WSS certificates, firewall/NAT rules, provider credentials/quotas, additional browser engines, relay TLS (turns:), long-session expiry and combined outages need their own evidence. Coturn's loopback-peer exception is enabled only in the isolated local fixture, not prescribed for production.
